Walk the Line

Walk the Line

You are paid by the meter.

Evidence in. A signed number out.

You are the general contractor

A general contractor is built to see everything, manage everything, and deliver inside the parameters — and those parameters get simplified to one number. Every stage is a different crew, proving what it did its own way. Assembling that into something one person can sign is the job, and it is the part no single trade owns.

What we are proposing to build

The four layers

Field
No app. A phone and a walk. One video, IMG_2104.MOV, 404.1 s, sha256 6ef62977…a3debf, and 53 HEIC photographs, every one carrying EXIF GPS.
Laptop
Python 3, OpenCV and NumPy, run locally and offline. One frame per second gives 405 frames; an HSV threshold against the APWA Uniform Color Code, morphological open then close, external contours, MIN_AREA_PX 900, and only the bottom 45% of frame considered (GROUND_FRACTION 0.45). That yields 124 colour regions. Seven deterministic rules in locates/classify.py then reject 122 of them. No model. No network. No API key.
Edge
A Cloudflare Worker, walk-the-line-api, compatibility date 2026-09-19, on workers.dev. A KV namespace bound as DECISIONS (beaf758828d7407a86d27c83685cb875) holds the decision log.
Consumers
A static mirror on GitHub Pages, branch gh-pages, and a separate app on Replit behind a sign-in.

What the edge serves

/locates/map/v1/v1/summary/v1/proposal /v1/checks/v1/evidence/v1/rules GET|POST /v1/decisionsPOST /v1/vision

/v1/checks is already shaped as the consuming app's EvidenceCheck[] — {code, passed, severity, message} — so there is no mapping layer to write on either side.

The decision log

Every decision is hashed with SHA-256 through crypto.subtle. Each entry stores the previous entry's hash and its own, computed as sha256(prevHash + JSON.stringify(entry)). A head key in KV holds {seq, hash}. Reading the log walks the chain and reports chainIntact. There are 4 entries today and the chain is intact.

The refusal path

A POST without a reviewer returns HTTP 400: “reviewer is required — an unsigned decision is not a decision”. A refusal requires a reason. Refusals are kept beside confirmations and are never deleted. A correction is a new link in the chain, never an edit.

The log is open, deliberately

POST /v1/decisions takes no key. Anyone with the URL can write to the chain, and that was a decision, not an oversight — a judge who cannot sign it themselves cannot test the one claim this project is built on. The cost is real: the log will accept a name that is not yours. It enforces that a decision is signed and reasoned, not that the signer is who they say they are. Authentication is the first thing to add before anyone bills from this.

Built, and blocked

The Workers AI binding [ai] is declared, and POST /v1/vision is written against @cf/meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct. Calling it returns 5016: Prior to using this model, you must submit the prompt 'agree' — the Meta licence, which requires representing non-EU domicile. It is built. It is not enabled. Nothing on this slide came out of it.

Seven independent votes, not a sieve

Every one of the 124 regions is put to all seven rules. They do not run in sequence and they do not partition the rejections — each votes on its own, so a region can be thrown out by several at once. These counts overlap by design: they sum to 232 firings over 122 rejected regions, about 2.1 rules apiece. Of the 47 rejections published as evidence, only 11 were rejected by a single rule; 22 by two, 12 by three, 2 by four.

on_pavementrejected98

pigment_coherencerejected18
not_a_slabrejected1
flat_filmrejected0

Each rule records what it removed, so a region thrown out by more than one rule is counted by each of them — these do not sum to the total. Out of 124 regions: 122 rejected, 2 candidates, 0 confirmed. No model, no network, no API key was involved in any of it.

What we already know is wrong

The saturation floor is too high

SAT_MEAN_MIN 110 carries the comment “locate paint is fluorescent”. Most real locate paint is faded, so it sits below that floor and is thrown away before any other rule gets a look at it. This is the single biggest reason the confirmed count is zero.

Green and yellow are mis-rejected

not_vegetation rejects green and yellow on excess-green arithmetic, which cannot tell green paint from grass. In source it now escalates those two colours to human review instead — and that change is deliberately not published, because adding a third verdict would silently change what a consuming app reads. The fix waits on the contract, not the other way round.

It was hunting the wrong colour

After the build, all 53 photographs were judged one at a time by eye and the verdicts written to locates/photo_truth.json: 26 carry locate paint, 16 are the hackathon venue, 5 are people, 6 are clear ground. The colours actually on the ground: red 19, green 10, yellow 3, white 2, orange 1. The detector's commonest find was orange — 63 of its 124 regions.

Measured, and derived

Building footprints and the street network come from OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API. Photograph positions are EXIF GPS: measured. Video reading positions are reconstructed along the block perimeter — 311 m over 404.1 s, 0.77 m/s, from one GPS anchor, ±7 m: derived. The two are carried separately through every layer and the derived ones are never presented as survey.

The mirror, and the consumer

The static mirror on gh-pages carries index.html (the raw-output map), /api/*.json, 45 frames and 26 photographs — so the evidence stands up with the Worker switched off. The consuming app is a separate thing on Replit, behind a sign-in, and it reads /v1/checks directly.

Why the distinction on every marker matters

It was hunting the wrong colour

What the detector matched · 124 colour regions in the video

orange 63yellow 24green 19blue 9red 6other 3

What is on the ground · 26 photographs, judged by eye

red 19green 10yellow 3white 2orange 1

It spent the afternoon chasing orange. The block is marked in red and green. Nothing was wrong with the rules; the question they were asked was wrong, and that is the whole reason recall was zero.

Withdrawn

This page previously said “orange dominating is what a fiber job should look like.” That was inferred from a tally without opening a single frame. It is withdrawn. Orange dominates because San Francisco has a great deal of terracotta.

Seven rules, one sieve

All 124 colour regions are put to all seven rules. They are not a cascade — each votes independently on every region, so a region can be rejected by several at once, and these counts overlap by design: on_pavement 98, stroke_width 51, not_vegetation 43, ground_band 21, pigment_coherence 18, not_a_slab 1. They sum to 232 firings over 122 rejected regions — 2.1 rules apiece, and only 11 of the 47 published rejections were thrown out by a single rule. flat_film ran over all 124 and rejected none; it stays in, measured and reported, until it earns its place. Two regions survive every rule. Past the desk the line runs pale and empty — nothing was booked.

The one we have to check first

The second frame in the rejected tray carries a green locate line along a slab joint. The green region the detector matched in that frame was thrown out partly by not_vegetation — it read green as chlorophyll. We have not proved the region it matched and the line in the picture are the same pixels. That is the first thing the next pass has to settle.

Each rule votes to reject on its own and carries the measurement that caused it, so a rejection is arguable rather than scored. The mailbox reads 194.9 px inscribed radius against a limit of 15.1. A reviewer can argue with that. Nobody can argue with a confidence of 0.05.

Nothing learned, nothing over the network: geometry and statistics over the same pixels. Status moves captured → proposed → needs_review → confirmed / refused, nothing auto-commits, and the audit trail is append-only in the database, not in a prompt — a Postgres trigger raises on any UPDATE or DELETE of an audit event.

VerdictAwaiting a humanhuman

An adjudication screen asks four things of any evidence: what is it, when was it taken, has it been altered, what does it cover. A verdict alone answers none of them, and evidence that is not attached to a proposal dead-ends — so every exhibit arrives carrying the proposal’s id.

The second opinion we lost

The design calls for two independent detectors. The Memories.ai half was built and never ran, on a $0 balance. A model asked “is there locate paint here?” would have said no to a mailbox immediately. Its absence is visible in the output.

The honest limit

Every threshold here is calibrated on the reject side. This clip produced no confirmed true positives, so nothing above shows the detector can recognise a real mark — only that it refuses things that plainly are not one. The 26 photographs prove the paint was there to find. The next clip has to be that block, with the thresholds pointed at red and green.
